english.notes:
(i) The date of the offence is the actual date of death.
(ii) The rule that death must follow within a year and a day applies to acts or omissions before 16th September 1996.
(iii) The rule is abolished for acts or omissions on or after that date which result in death. See the Abolition - 'year and a day rule'
(iv) The consent of the Attorney General is required where:-
(a) the injury was sustained more than three years before death; OR
(b) the accused has been previously convicted of the offence alleged to be connected with the death.
(v) See also offence wording: H2169 which relates to manslaughter.
(vi) Officers should carefully check an offender's previous convictions. Provisions under sections 224 to 235 of the Criminal Justice Act 2003 may mean that s/he is liable to receive a longer sentence if certain conditions apply.
(vii) The CPS have issued guidance for murder and manslaughter.
(viii) Where this offence is committed against an emergency worker this must be treated as an aggravating factor in sentencing, see section 67 of the Sentencing Act 2020. The provisions requiring a life sentence do not apply where a person suffers from diminished responsibility, see sections 258A(4), 274A and 285A(4).
(ix) Terrorist connection - this offence is listed in Schedule 1 to the Sentencing Act 2020. Where the court has determined that there is a terrorist connection, the court has to treat this as an aggravating factor in sentencing (section 69 of that Act) and the notification requirements under the Counter-Terrorism Act 2008 apply (section 42 of that Act). In addition, section 23A of the Terrorism Act 2000 provides for forfeiture of money or other property.
(x) See section 72 of the Domestic Abuse Act 2021 regarding the committing of this offence outside the UK by a UK national or a person habitually resident in England and Wales.
